panels.description: Per attempt, buffered path, upstream 2xx only â€” retry backoff and every gateway refusal are excluded. The honest reading for "is the provider slow".
panels.title: Upstream latency P50 / P95 / P99 (successful attempts)

panels.description: The gap is gateway overhead: retry backoff plus rate-limit wait. Read the gap, not either line. request_duration_seconds has no status label and is observed for refusals too â€” sheds included, which carry real provider names and land near 0s â€” so heavy shedding pulls it DOWN and the two lines cross. The upstream line is the clean one.
panels.title: Client-observed vs upstream latency (P95)

panels.description: status is a category â€” 2xx|4xx|429|5xx, with 429 carved out of 4xx. provider="unknown" covers requests rejected before provider resolution (bad JSON, missing model): client errors, not gateway faults. An open breaker hides inside 5xx â€” read the breaker panel alongside.
panels.title: Success rate (by provider)

panels.description: Do NOT sum these. shed = the gateway is out of capacity (operator problem, every caller affected); rate limited = one caller over quota (expected). Both also land inside requests_total{status="429"}, and upstream 429s do too, so 429s cannot be decomposed from requests_total alone. A breaker refusal has no counter of its own â€” it only appears in 5xx.
panels.title: Refusals: capacity vs quota vs breaker

panels.description: MAX_IN_FLIGHT is an env var, not a metric, so the ceiling cannot be queried â€” the thresholds and axis max below assume the default 256 and are retuned by hand if the env var is. Saturation here predicts shedding before shed_total moves.
panels.title: In-flight occupancy vs the ceiling

panels.description: 0=closed, 1=half-open, 2=open. Every provider gets a series from its first served request, so a flat 0 means observed-healthy rather than never-observed. A provider that has never served a request has no series â€” by design: the registry, not the breaker group, decides which providers exist.
panels.title: Circuit breaker state (by provider)

panels.description: An aborted stream is otherwise invisible: the header left with the first frame, so requests_total already recorded a 2xx and the failure reaches the client as an in-band SSE frame no counter sees. upstream_idle = the provider went quiet; write_idle = the client stopped reading. absolute_max is different in kind â€” it only fires once both inactivity bounds failed to, so any value means the protection itself is broken. Treat it as a bug report, not a trend.
